Plex (Free trial, Plex Pass subscription required after) with the Plex server installed on my computer paired with a Chromecast is by far my most used app. You have to have a subscription now for the app after a trial period, but I was grandfathered in for buying it when it was a paid app.

Screen Filter (Free) is my go to screen dimming app. It doesn't have a fancy interface, but it works and has been compatible with all of my devices.

VLC for Android (Free) is probably the best video player on Android that I've used. I am never fond of the built-in apps, and they even have a dark theme which is easier on the eyes.

Remote Control (Free, by Google) is great if you use Chrome on your computer and install the matching Chrome extension. I work from home, so when I need to get ready but don't want to get out of bed, I use this to get all of my tools ready. I also use it while travelling to access my computer.

Call Recorder (Paid - $9.95 USD) may be a bit controversial, but I have used it on multiple devices flawlessly. Root is not always required, but recommended. I disable the notifications so it always records silently. This may not be legal to use in your area, so use with caution. You can get a trial before buying to see if it works on your device. There are multiple recording methods, but the automatic detection has never failed me.

Blacked Out! (Free) is a CM12 theme that works great on my AMOLED devices. I haven't run into any of the black-text-on-black issues in quite a few versions. You must be using CM12 or newer ROM that includes the theme engine.

Apex Launcher (Free, paid version available) always ends up as my default launcher. I know a lot of people prefer Nova, but Apex has always felt a little more streamlined to me. It's very customizable and the vast majority of features are available in the free version.

Velur Icon Pack (Paid, $0.99 USD) always seems to be on sale. It's been in the rotation of icon packs that I use with Apex for a long time, and I love the look.

I love open source applications, so F-Droid is the only non-Play Store app I use. Everything is free, and seeing how few permissions are required really makes me question how much data is gathered by most apps in the Play Store. The following are all found on F-Droid and some require root. None have advertisements or in-app purchases.

AFWall+ (Requires root) is my go-to firewall app since DroidWall was discontinued. It requires some work when setting up a new device, but it notifies you by default to allow apps thorugh when you install them.

AdAway (Requires root) is the best ad-blocking app I've used on Android. Many of the ones that rely on proxy servers tend to cause pages to load slowly. Once it downalods and applies the blocklist, I never see an ad again.

2048 (no root) is a simple game that has somehow kept me addicted after the hype. This one is free, no ads, quick, and no extra bloat or online features.

Air-Share and Air-launch (Free - made for Android TV)

Air-Launch is designed to launch apps remotely and sideload APKs on devices like Android TV using your phone or tablet. Air-Launch is part of the Air-Share App but appears as a separate app icon for convenience. I used this app for sideloading apks on the Nexus Player and it was great!

Google Opinion Rewards (Free) Complete surveys to earn Google Play credits. I certainly find it slowed down since months ago but I still get a couple free bucks here!
Weather Timeline($0.99) The best material design weather app I've come across. Rain alert notifications. Material widget. Uses forecast.io for accurate local weather.
I've found Weather Timeline to be the only weather app that is aesthetically pleasing and pragmatic.
